valuation.method: Valuation floors (earnings power x multiple): NVDA's own point-in-time multiple history, peer trough multiples, consensus and historical earnings drawdowns, cash-flow and earnings-yield floors
valuation.headline: Valuation gives three tiers below $162.85: about $131-142 (-13% to -19%) if earnings hold and the multiple falls to NVDA's own record low (17.0x trailing, Dec 2018) or the 2022 peer-trough forward multiple; about $93-119 (-27% to -43%) if trailing earnings are priced like a cyclical semiconductor at its trough (about 12x) or stripped of non-operating gains; and $46-88 only if earnings also fall by the 48-56% seen in NVDA's 2019 and 2023 downturns while the multiple stays at trough, a combination with no NVDA precedent. Today's price already assumes roughly no growth beyond trailing EPS at a market multiple (about half of FY2028 consensus), but it does not price an actual decline in earnings.

levels.label: Peer-trough forward multiple on unchanged consensus (AVGO, Oct 2022)
levels.basis: AVGO minimum quarter-end forward P/E 11.737x (2022-10-30) x NVDA NTM consensus EPS 12.097 (= 162.85 / stockanalysis forward P/E 13.4619) = 141.98. Same method: AMAT 12.783x -> 154.6; median of six peer minimums 11.16x -> 135.0.
levels.assumes: NTM consensus EPS of about 12.1 survives the 11-17 print and the governance/export news; the market pays NVDA what it paid Broadcom at the 2022 semiconductor low.
levels.breaks_if: Consensus is cut (Zacks FY2027 has only moved 9.62 -> 9.28 in 7 days, FY2028 rose), or the multiple goes to the lower peer troughs (QCOM 9.5x, INTC 10.6x, MU 6.5x).
levels.sources: stockanalysis ratios quarterly (AVGO, NVDA); 20 quarter-end observations per ticker

levels.label: NVDA's own record-low trailing P/E on trailing GAAP EPS
levels.basis: Lowest daily point-in-time trailing P/E in the 10-year price file: 16.97x on 2018-12-24 (close 3.177 / TTM diluted EPS 0.18725, quarter ended 2018-10-28, filed 2018-11-15); 17.09x on 2019-01-03 is the minimum of the 2019+ window. 16.97 x TTM GAAP EPS 7.91 = 134.23. AVGO trailing trough 17.07x gives 135.0.
levels.assumes: Trailing GAAP EPS of 7.91 is not about to fall; the market repeats the multiple it paid when it believed NVDA earnings had peaked in late 2018.
levels.breaks_if: Trailing EPS is restated lower in investors' minds (non-GAAP TTM is 7.01, see $119), or the market treats NVDA like commodity semiconductors (about 12x trailing at troughs). An in-line Q3 moves this floor up: non-GAAP TTM becomes 8.20 and 16.97x gives 139.
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR companyfacts TTM EPS by filing date; /home/user/Temp/.cache/nvda_daily10y.pkl

levels.label: 4% trailing free-cash-flow yield
levels.basis: TTM FCF 127.006B / 24.147B shares = 5.26 per share; 5.26 / 0.04 = 131.49. Current FCF yield 3.23%.
levels.assumes: TTM FCF is representative. It is only 66% of TTM net income (127.0B vs 192.9B); latest quarter FCF 21.4B vs net income 59.7B.
levels.breaks_if: Cash conversion normalises upward (floor rises) or working capital and supply prepayments keep absorbing cash (floor falls).
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR TTM cash flow; stockanalysis statistics (shares, FCF per share 5.26)

levels.label: NVDA's own record-low EV/EBITDA on trailing EBITDA
levels.basis: Lowest daily EV/EBITDA (market cap + debt - cash - short-term investments): 14.92x on 2018-12-24. (14.92 x EBITDA 201.266B + net cash 23.609B) / 24.147B shares = 125.34. On the cash-only EV definition used in NVDA.evseries.json the trough is 16.35x -> 137.3.
levels.assumes: TTM EBITDA of 201.3B holds; 2018 trough multiple repeats.
levels.breaks_if: EBITDA falls (it fell 48% peak to trough in both 2018-19 and 2022-23), or peer-trough EV/EBITDA applies (AVGO 11.5x -> 96.6; median of eight peers 9.4x -> 79.7).
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR TTM series; price file; stockanalysis statistics (net cash, shares)

levels.label: Record-low trailing P/E on trailing non-GAAP EPS
levels.basis: 16.97x x non-GAAP TTM EPS 7.01 (Zacks: 1.30 + 1.62 + 1.87 + 2.22) = 118.96. Equivalent grid cell: 15x x TTM GAAP 7.91 = 118.7.
levels.assumes: Investors discard the non-operating gains in GAAP earnings (GAAP net income 58.3B exceeded operating income 53.5B in fiscal Q1) and pay the 2018 trough multiple.
levels.breaks_if: Q3 on 11-17 is in line (non-GAAP TTM 8.20 -> 139 at the same multiple) or misses and guides down (floor falls with EPS).
levels.sources: Zacks detailed estimates (EPS TTM, surprise history); SEC TTM series; stockanalysis quarterly income figures

levels.label: Low-end peer-trough forward multiple on unchanged consensus (QCOM, Sep 2022)
levels.basis: QCOM minimum quarter-end forward P/E 9.53x (2022-09-25) x NTM EPS 12.097 = 115.29. Nearby cells: earnings yield of 10-year + 3 points on FY2027 consensus = 9.28 / 0.081 = 114.6; 15x x (FY2027 consensus -20% = 7.42) = 111.4; INTC 10.58x x NTM = 128.0.
levels.assumes: Consensus holds but NVDA is valued as a mature, legally encumbered chip franchise (Qualcomm in 2022).
levels.breaks_if: Growth continues near consensus (FY2028 EPS 15.73 puts this price at 7.3x), or estimates are cut so the same multiple gives less.
levels.sources: stockanalysis ratios quarterly (QCOM, INTC, NVDA); Zacks; FRED DGS10

levels.label: 5% trailing free-cash-flow yield
levels.assumes: TTM FCF 127.0B is the right base and the market demands a yield near the 10-year Treasury (5.10%).
levels.breaks_if: FCF converges toward net income (consensus FY2027 FCF 189.8B on stockanalysis would give 157 at 5%).
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR TTM cash flow; stockanalysis statistics and forecast; FRED DGS10

levels.label: Trailing earnings yield = 10-year Treasury + 3 points (no growth needed)
levels.assumes: Price at which trailing GAAP earnings alone pay an equity-like premium over Treasuries with zero growth.
levels.breaks_if: Trailing earnings fall rather than stay flat; or the 10-year yield moves.
levels.sources: FRED DGS10; SEC TTM EPS; stockanalysis ratios (AVGO)

levels.label: Cyclical-semiconductor trough multiple on trailing earnings (median of 8 peer trailing P/E minimums, 11.8x)
levels.basis: Peer minimum quarter-end trailing P/E: AMD 45.08, ASML 28.12, AVGO 17.07, AMAT 11.83, TSM 11.71, QCOM 10.96, INTC 7.96, MU 7.28; median 11.77 x 7.91 = 93.11. Identical grid cells: 10x x FY2027 consensus 9.28 = 92.8; 20x x (FY2027 -50% = 4.64) = 92.8.
levels.assumes: The market decides current earnings are cycle-peak and pays what it paid TSM, AMAT and QCOM at their 2022 lows.
levels.breaks_if: Earnings keep growing (peak-earnings multiples are only applied when a decline is expected); or earnings really do fall, in which case see the tiers below.
levels.sources: stockanalysis ratios quarterly for 8 peers, 20 quarters each (late 2021 to Q3 2026); SEC TTM EPS

levels.label: 6% trailing free-cash-flow yield
levels.assumes: TTM FCF flat; market demands about 0.9 point over the 10-year yield in cash.
levels.breaks_if: Same as other FCF floors: conversion is currently depressed relative to earnings.
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR TTM cash flow; stockanalysis statistics

levels.label: Double trough: NVDA-sized earnings drawdown at NVDA's record-low multiple
levels.basis: 17.5x x (FY2027 consensus 9.28 x 0.5 = 4.64) = 81.2. Exact precedent inputs: 16.97x x 9.28 x (1 - 0.478) = 82.2; 16.97x x TTM 7.91 x (1 - 0.558) = 59.4. Nearby: trailing earnings yield of 10-year + 5 points (10.1%, 9.9x) = 78.3; median peer trough EV/EBITDA 9.44x = 79.7.
levels.assumes: Earnings power halves, as TTM EPS did in 2018-19 (-47.8%) and FY2022-23 (-55.8%), taking EPS back to about FY2026's level (4.77 non-GAAP), and the market pays only a trough multiple on those trough earnings.
levels.breaks_if: History: at the 2018 and 2022 price lows NVDA traded at 32.5x and 66x the eventual trough EPS, because the market looked through the dip. This cell needs the decline to be seen as structural (export bans, lost share, a collapse in customer spending), not cyclical.
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR annual and TTM EPS; Zacks consensus; FRED DGS10; stockanalysis peer ratios

levels.label: 8% trailing free-cash-flow yield
levels.assumes: Distressed-style cash yield on today's depressed FCF; effectively also assumes earnings fall toward FCF.
levels.breaks_if: Any normalisation of cash conversion; a net-cash company with 127B of FCF buying back stock at this yield.
levels.sources: SEC EDGAR TTM cash flow; stockanalysis statistics

levels.label: Arbitrary tail: 10x on halved earnings
levels.basis: 10x x 4.64 = 46.4. Not tied to any NVDA precedent; resembles INTC and MU trough trailing multiples (7.96x, 7.28x) applied to halved EPS (37 and 34).
levels.assumes: Earnings halve and NVDA is valued like the weakest large semiconductor franchises at their lows.
levels.breaks_if: Shown only to bound the grid; no documented case of NVDA trading below 17x trailing in the data read.
levels.sources: Grid arithmetic; stockanalysis ratios quarterly (INTC, MU)

caveats: Consensus is stale relative to the news. Zacks FY2027 was trimmed only from 9.62 to 9.28 in the last 7 days and FY2028 rose to 15.73; earnings on 2026-11-17 (after the close) and the first guidance under the interim CEO will re-base every row. An in-line Q3 lifts non-GAAP TTM EPS from 7.01 to about 8.20 and raises trailing-multiple floors about 17%; a guide-down lowers them.
GAAP TTM EPS (7.91) is above non-GAAP (7.01) because GAAP includes non-operating gains (fiscal Q1 net income 58.3B vs operating income 53.5B). Floors built on 7.91 are flattered by about 11%.

TTM free cash flow (127.0B) is 66% of net income (192.9B), and the latest quarter was 21.4B against 59.7B of net income, so FCF-yield floors sit well below earnings-based floors and move a lot if cash conversion changes.

The 'FY2027 cut by 20/35/50%' rows cannot literally happen to fiscal 2027: the first half (4.09) is reported and Q3 has ended. Read them as haircuts to forward earnings power; -50% is roughly a return to FY2026 EPS (4.77 non-GAAP, 4.90 GAAP).

NVDA's own precedents cut both ways. In 2018 and 2022 the price bottomed at a low multiple of peak earnings (17.0x and 29.2x), which was 32.5x and 66x the eventual trough EPS, so multiplying a trough multiple by trough earnings double-counts relative to history. But in both cases the growth story and management were intact; a governance, legal or export-control shock that impairs the franchise is outside those precedents.

Peer evidence is thin: 20 quarter-end snapshots per ticker (late 2021 to Q3 2026), covering one downturn (2022) and missing intra-quarter lows. AMD and INTC trailing P/E are distorted by small or negative GAAP earnings; MU's forward P/E shows a repeated 203.0 placeholder in five loss-making quarters, which inflates its median.

A valuation floor is not support. Multiples have no hard lower bound (MU forward P/E 4.4x today, INTC 8.0x trailing in 2022), and no EPS scenario here includes legal or regulatory penalties; for scale, each $10B of fines or settlements is about $0.41 per share.

Point-in-time dating uses 10-Q/10-K filing dates, which trail the earnings release by days to weeks, so trough multiples around report dates are approximate. The evseries EV nets cash only (not short-term investments), overstating EV by about 1%; stockanalysis shows 19.42x against 19.55x.
This is analysis of what stated assumptions imply, not a forecast or advice.

options.method: Options-implied (risk-neutral) distribution from the full NVDA option chain on Nasdaq's public option-chain endpoint: 24 expiries (2026-11-16 to 2029-01-19), 2,232 strike rows, closing quotes of Friday 2026-11-13 with spot $162.85. Prices are bid/ask mids (ask-only -> half the ask; last as final fallback); 155 Dec-2026 rows with strikes above $480 and no bid/ask were dropped. For each expiry: (1) ATM straddle interpolated at spot (linear in strike, and re-priced at K=spot from the interpolated ATM IV) -> implied move in $ and %, and a 1-SD range S*exp(+/-IV*sqrt(T)); (2) implied vols: puts inverted with a 200-step American binomial tree, calls with Black-Scholes, T = calendar days/365, r from FRED DTB3 (4.14% discount = 4.22% continuous) for expiries up to 3 months and interpolated to DGS1/DGS2 beyond, q = 0.614% from the collected stockanalysis statistics; skew read at strikes 10/20/30% below spot; (3) risk-neutral probability of finishing below each level = e^(rT) x slope of put price in strike, computed two ways: raw finite differences of quoted put mids across neighbouring strikes, and (primary) the derivative of European put prices re-generated from a spread-weighted smoothing spline through the de-Americanised put IVs; quantiles are read off the same curve; (4) earnings-day move isolated by subtracting the pre-earnings (Nov-16) variance and an assumed ordinary Tuesday from the first post-earnings (Nov-18) variance; (5) put open interest and Friday volume by strike. Scripts and intermediate files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Temp/dbacb4e2-62a8-5da8-88f5-6a2f24aae003/scratchpad/nvda/ (fetch_chain.py, analyze2.py, metrics.py, metrics_term.json).
options.headline: As of Friday's close (before the 2026-11-17 report) options price a +/-8.6% ($14) move through Wednesday's first post-earnings expiry, about +/-7% of it from the earnings reaction itself; the one-standard-deviation downside is about $146 this week, $136 by Dec 18, $131 by mid-January and $113 by June 2027, with the risk-neutral 5% tail at about $135 this week, $117 by Dec 18, $108 by January and $78 by June 2027. A close below the $148.80 low is priced at about 20% by Wednesday and 31% by Dec 18; a close below $100 at about 1.6% by Dec 18, 3% by January, 11% by June 2027 and 27% by January 2029 -- risk-neutral odds, which overstate real-world odds when protection is bid.

levels.label: 1-SD downside by Mon 2026-11-16 close (last expiry before earnings)
levels.basis: Nov-16 ATM IV 49.4% (average of call and put IV at the $162.5/$165 strikes, interpolated to spot), T=3/365 -> IV*sqrt(T)=4.48%; 162.85*exp(-0.0448)=155.72. ATM straddle $5.82 = 3.6%. Risk-neutral 16% quantile $155.8; P(close<$150)=4.3%, P(<$148.80)=3.2%, P(<$140) about 0.4%.
levels.assumes: No new shock before Monday's close larger than Friday's option prices allow for; lognormal 1-SD from ATM IV.
levels.breaks_if: A fresh headline (charges, subpoena, pre-announcement) lands before the report; the market still puts about 1-in-25 odds on a Monday close below $150.
levels.sources: Nasdaq option-chain API, expiry 2026-11-16 (retrieved 2026-11-15T02:55Z); FRED DTB3; stockanalysis dividend yield

levels.label: Heaviest put strike (positioning concentration, not a floor)
levels.basis: $150 puts carry the largest put open interest summed over all expiries: 636,808 contracts (183,265 in Jan-2027, 42,115 in Nov-20, 38,603 in Dec-18, 13,924 in Nov-16). On Friday $160 puts had the largest volume (223,333 across expiries) and $150 the second (168,652); 49.3% of Friday's put volume in expiries through Jan-2027 was in strikes $150-$162.85 and 15.7% in $140-$150.
levels.assumes: Open-interest concentration marks where hedges and dealer gamma sit, so price action tends to be busiest around it.
levels.breaks_if: OI does not show who is long or short; if dealers are short these puts, hedging adds to selling through $150 rather than supporting it. OI shown may predate Friday's trades.
levels.sources: Nasdaq option-chain API, all 24 expiries (retrieved 2026-11-15T02:55-02:56Z)

levels.label: 1-SD downside from the earnings reaction alone (range $148.4-$149.2; coincides with the $148.80 52-week low)
levels.basis: Total ATM variance Nov-18 0.011694 minus Nov-16 0.002005 minus an assumed ordinary Tuesday (0.002005 if Tue=Mon; 0.00146 if Tue=average of Thu/Fri after earnings; 0.00108 if Tue=average session of Nov 23-27) = 0.00768-0.00861 -> 1-SD 8.8-9.3% ($14.3-$15.1), expected absolute move 7.0-7.4% ($11.4-$12.1). 162.85*exp(-0.0907)=148.73 (middle case).
levels.assumes: ATM variance adds across days; Tuesday is an ordinary pre-earnings day (no Tuesday expiry exists to measure it); spot still near $162.85 going into the print.
levels.breaks_if: Spot moves on Monday/Tuesday headlines before the report; the report or the CEO/investigation commentary produces a move beyond 1 SD (about a 1-in-6 one-sided event by construction).
levels.sources: Nasdaq option-chain API, expiries 2026-11-16, 11-18, 11-20, 11-27

caveats: These are risk-neutral probabilities: they embed the premium investors pay for protection, so they overstate real-world odds of decline when puts are bid (as now, with 13 downgrades, an investigation and earnings ahead). The low long-dated medians ($150 for Jan-2029) are mostly volatility drag in a lognormal-like distribution, not a forecast of decline.
Everything is as of Friday 2026-11-13 closing quotes, before the 2026-11-17 after-close report; the whole surface will reprice on Monday headlines and again after earnings.

Finishing below a level at expiry is not the same as touching it. The chance of trading through a level at some point before expiry is higher -- up to roughly double for a driftless diffusion (reflection-principle rule of thumb, not measured from quotes). Example: about 20% to close below $148.80 on Wednesday is consistent with something like a 30-40% chance of printing below it by then.

Quote quality: closing snapshot with some crossed bid/ask pairs; ask-only quotes were valued at half the ask. Thin areas: Nov-16 puts below about $142 (5 cents or less), most weekly puts below $100-$105, Dec-18 below $90, and 2028-2029 LEAPS generally. Near/mid-dated probabilities are good to about +/-1-2 points, 2028-2029 to +/-3-5 points; 1% quantiles are rough.

Model choices: puts de-Americanised with a 200-step binomial tree, calls treated as European; T in calendar days/365 (the Monday expiry carries the weekend: 49.4% calendar IV is about 71% on a one-trading-day basis). I used DTB3 for expiries up to 3 months and interpolated to DGS1/DGS2 beyond rather than a flat DTB3; with flat DTB3 no probability changes by more than 0.13 points.

Dividend input: 0.614% yield from the collected data. Long-dated put-call parity fits better with a carry closer to q = 0 (Jan-2029 ATM put IV 43.8% vs call IV 46.6% at q=0.614%, 44.4% vs 44.9% at q=0); switching to q=0 moves probabilities by at most 0.33 points, so conclusions are unaffected.

The earnings-day isolation depends on what Tuesday is assumed to be worth, because there is no Tuesday expiry; the three baselines give 7.0-7.4% expected absolute move. The 4-session count for Nov 23-27 assumes the US Thanksgiving closure on Thu Nov 26 (remembered calendar fact; consistent with the chain listing no Nov-26 expiry).
One-SD ranges use ATM IV and a symmetric lognormal; with put skew the true downside tail is fatter -- use the quantile table (T4) for tails.

Open interest does not show direction (who is long or short), so heavy-OI strikes are not floors. The open interest shown may be as of the prior session (some Nov-16 strikes show volume but blank OI); I could not verify the OI as-of date from the page.

Spot of $162.85 is the stock close; near-dated put-call parity implies the option market closed about $0.10-$0.25 lower (parity forward $162.74 vs $162.90 for Nov-16), which is immaterial to the probabilities because they come from put-price slopes.
Analysis, not advice.
